evals.prompt: hey, i'm training for my first half marathon, it's in 12 weeks. can you help me out?
evals.expected_output: Claude should recognize this as a fresh goal with no existing /areas/ file, and run through Setup conversationally (not as a rigid form): gather the goal/date/objective, current fitness, constraints/injuries, logistics, and available data sources. It should NOT immediately generate a full 12-week training plan before gathering this context. It should NOT claim to have created files or connected tools it hasn't actually used.
expectations: Recognizes no existing goal exists in memory and treats this as a fresh Setup, not a plan request
Does not produce a full multi-week training plan in this response
Asks about the athlete's objective (finish / finish strong / specific target), not just the event and date
Asks about injury history directly rather than waiting for it to surface
Asks what data sources (health connector, manual reporting) are available rather than assuming
Does not claim to have written memory files or connected a tool it has not actually used
Reads as a real conversational interview, not a rigid form dump of every question at once

evals.prompt: just finished my long run, 14km, took about 1h20. felt good, no issues.
evals.expected_output: Claude should check whether a health/fitness connector is available before commenting on pace/HR. If no connector, it should say so plainly (not silently trust the self-report as verified data) and offer to log what was reported. It should attempt to read recent /workouts/ entries for comparison if any exist. It should not fabricate metrics (HR, splits) that weren't provided or pulled from a real source.
expectations: States plainly that no data connector is available rather than silently treating the self-report as verified data
Does not fabricate HR, splits, or other metrics that were not provided
References at least one prior /workouts/ entry for comparison (the 10km and 12km long runs already logged)
Does not ask for a data source a second time given the athlete already described the session in the message
Offers to log the session or logs it, consistent with 'log only what's confirmed'

evals.prompt: did today's tempo run but I ran it way faster than prescribed because I was feeling great
evals.expected_output: Claude should name the deviation explicitly (ran faster than prescribed) BEFORE assessing whether it's good or bad. It should check the /areas/ file for the athlete's stated objective and any standing pacing constraints, and reference the goal hierarchy if going faster conflicts with the training purpose (e.g. a controlled progression plan). It should not simply praise the faster pace without first flagging that it deviated from plan.
expectations: Names the deviation (ran faster than the prescribed tempo pace) explicitly before offering any assessment of whether it's good or bad
References the athlete's actual stated objective from the area file (controlled progression / history of blowing up late) rather than a generic 'faster is better' take
Connects today's deviation to the standing note about this athlete's specific pattern of overcooking tempo runs when feeling good
Does not simply praise the faster pace without first flagging that it deviated from plan

evals.prompt: my knee felt a little off during squats today but I pushed through, it's probably fine
evals.expected_output: Claude should check /areas/ for any existing knee-related constraint. If one exists, it should treat this report as touching that standing constraint and NOT let 'probably fine' from the athlete override the flag -- it should note it, ask follow-up questions, and suggest appropriate caution, without being alarmist. It should not simply agree it's probably fine and move on.
expectations: Checks memory and identifies the existing left-knee patellar tendon watch-item from the area file
Does not accept 'probably fine' as the last word on a report that touches a known standing constraint
Asks a genuine follow-up question (e.g. where exactly, sharp vs dull, whether it changed during the session, how it feels now, or whether warm-up was done per the standing rule)
Suggests appropriate caution (e.g. modifying load, watching the next session) without being alarmist or catastrophizing
Does not simply agree it's probably fine and move on without engaging the constraint

evals.prompt: can you set up my workouts for next week on my calendar? monday/wednesday/friday, easy runs
evals.expected_output: Claude should check the calendar tool for existing conflicts before proposing times, and write full session instructions into the event body (not just a title like 'Easy run'). If it references a standing constraint or plan detail, it should be accurate to what's actually in memory, not invented. After creating events, it should summarize the week in prose.
expectations: Checks for a calendar tool/connector and existing conflicts before proposing or creating times, rather than assuming availability
If it creates or proposes events, writes full session instructions into the event body rather than only a bare title like 'Easy run'
Any plan detail or standing constraint it references (e.g. the warm-up rule, preferred morning time) is accurate to what's actually in the area file, not invented
Summarizes the week in prose after proposing/creating the sessions rather than leaving only a wall of raw events
If no calendar tool is actually available in this environment, says so plainly rather than pretending to have created events

evals.prompt: wait, I don't think that's right -- I ran on Tuesday not Wednesday
evals.expected_output: This tests the correction protocol. Claude should acknowledge the error plainly and briefly, re-derive/correct without over-apologizing or excessive hedging, and continue the conversation normally rather than becoming defensive or overly cautious in subsequent turns.
expectations: Acknowledges the date error plainly and briefly, without over-apologizing
Does not become defensive or excessively hedge
Fixes the underlying workout-log artifact itself (the existing logged entry with the wrong day), not just the conversational reply
Continues naturally afterward rather than derailing into extended meta-commentary about the mistake

evals.expected_output: This is a standalone factual question, not a session review. Claude should answer directly per the 'Answering a standalone question' section, without forcing it through the full session-review procedure (no need to check data sources, compare to history, etc.) unless genuinely relevant.
expectations: Answers the question directly and reasonably promptly
Does not force the response through the full session-review procedure (no unnecessary data-source checks, no forced comparison against training history)
Does not pad the answer with unrelated coaching-review content just because a goal exists in memory

evals.prompt: I've been lifting for years, pretty strong. Let's start my plan for the strongman comp in 10 weeks -- can you write me week 1?
evals.expected_output: Claude should NOT immediately draft week 1. It should recognize 'pretty strong' is not a benchmark and run the full Setup sequence: interview (goal/objective, fitness history, injuries -- asked directly, not skipped because the athlete sounds experienced), THEN benchmarking (ask for actual current numbers/maxes on the lifts the comp and plan will center on, preferring a safer submaximal test or an upload over a true 1RM), and only then move to drafting a plan. It should explain why it's asking rather than just writing the plan, if the athlete seems impatient.
expectations: Does not draft or output a week 1 plan in this response
Asks direct injury-history questions despite the athlete sounding experienced, rather than skipping them
Asks about the athlete's actual current objective for the comp (finish / place / hit a specific number)
Asks for actual current numbers on lifts central to the plan rather than accepting 'pretty strong' as a benchmark
If it asks for a max-effort test, prefers a safer proxy (e.g. 3RM, submaximal effort) over a true 1RM, and says why
Briefly explains why it's asking rather than just complying, given the athlete's evident impatience

evals.prompt: ok my goal is finishing a Hyrox in 4 months, I used to run track in college but haven't trained seriously in 6 years, no current injuries but I tore my ACL in college
evals.expected_output: Claude should treat 'tore my ACL in college' as a real constraint even though it's old and the athlete didn't flag it as current -- this tests that old/dismissed injuries get captured, not just present-tense ones. It should distinguish the fitness history (college track, 6 years inactive) from current fitness level, and should move to benchmarking next rather than assuming college-level fitness still applies.
expectations: Explicitly captures the old ACL tear as a constraint/watch-item despite the athlete framing it as past and not currently injured
Distinguishes fitness history (college track background) from current fitness level, and does not assume college-level fitness still applies after a 6-year layoff
Moves toward benchmarking current numbers/paces next rather than jumping straight to a plan
Does not brush past or drop the ACL mention just because the athlete downplayed it
